questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the teaching was in English and that I would have a day-to-day life at a hospital experiencing diseases and clinical manifestations I've only read about in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The exchange university was extremely helpful, so I was able to e-mail them when I had any question.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I hadn't recieved a welcome email from the university hopsital upon my arrival, but shortly after emailing the medical school I heard from them right away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a studio apartment before I arrived, which was very easy to move into - but it was also a bit expensive. Sydney has a lot of flatmate opportunities, if you're willing to search for a bit longer.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's crucial that you engage and seek out social events and gatherings, in that way you'll meet a lot of new friends even though you're not living with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wasn't offered housing by the University, since the medical exchange programme is only 3 months.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was quite a mouthful, but mainly because they needed a lot of health information and documentation in order for me to attend the clinical elective. Luckily the student counsellors from USYD were very helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mailing with student counsellors and a guide to completing the required documentation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend classes, but were at a clinical elective at three different departments of my own choosing.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time, ask for help whenever you need it, and remember that it will all be worth it in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical elective, pretty similar to a danish clinical elective.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit less independent work at the hospital compared to when you attend a clinical elective in Denmark, but is was mainly due to them having a totally different IT-system and way of rounding the patients.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical elective at three different departments, 1 month at each department.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not relevant.

questions.answer: Not relevant.

questions.answer: Not relevant, since I didn't spent time at the university itself, only the hospital.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spent as much time as possible exploring both Sydney but also north and south of Sydney. There are many beautiful national parks only a short car- or train-ride away. Also do take longer trips around Australia, you might as well when you've travelled that far. My biggest recommendation is going for a trip to the Northern Territory to visit the Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the Australian people is very open and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There's nothing that challenging coming to mind.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness, the humor and slight sarcasm, and the melting of many different cultures into one.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use the helpful student counselors at USYD, make sure to engage socially, and throw yourself into speaking English - I promise you that your English academic vocabulary will enhance greatly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though you live off campus, you can stille make a lot of friends. Try starting with catching up with other UCPH students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The independence and assertiveness I gained along during my stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first days where you were completely alone in a new big city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
